image_description: A grey whale surfaces in green ocean water, its dark, mottled back and dorsal knuckles visible just above the surface. In the background, a small boat filled with tourists wearing life jackets observes the whale. A person's head and shoulder are visible in the immediate foreground right.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The whale's head is submerged or obscured by the angle and water; only the posterior back and dorsal area are clearly visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the whale's back clearly displays the characteristic mottled grey skin with lighter, rough-textured patches consistent with barnacle infestations.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows a series of small humps (knuckles) along the ridge of the back instead of a single triangular dorsal fin, which is a definitive trait of the grey whale.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible section of the body appears thick and robust, consistent with the massive scale of a baleen whale relative to the nearby boat.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed on the visible dorsal surface; the texture and coloration match the biological description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The whale's mouth is closed and submerged; baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are located on the underside/lateral aspects and are not visible in this dorsal-view shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are not visible in the frame; the image captures the mid-to-posterior back.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The close-up view of the back reveals a non-smooth, textured surface consistent with callosities and barnacle clusters.

alignment_reasoning: All testable checkpoints are fully present. The image exhibits the definitive diagnostic features of a grey whale: specifically the absence of a dorsal fin replaced by dorsal knuckles, and the unique mottled grey skin with barnacle patches. Non-testable checkpoints are due to occlusion/angle, not absence. Class conformance is perfect.
artifact_reasoning: No AI-generation artifacts detected. The image displays natural photographic characteristics including realistic water dynamics, proper lighting/shadows, consistent depth of field, and biologically accurate anatomy without structural melting or boundary bleeding.
